# AnalystOS

> Reads a source document and returns a report in which every figure is a verified quote or an independently recomputed calculation, sealed so anyone can re-verify it offline. Early stage: use non-confidential documents only.

## API

- [OpenAPI 3.1](https://analystos.dev/api/v1/openapi.json): every endpoint, request and response
- [API index](https://analystos.dev/api/v1): machine-readable list of endpoints and limits
- [API guide](https://analystos.dev/docs/api.md): Endpoints, auth, configuration and limits of /api/v1

## Verifying a report

- [Seal specification](https://analystos.dev/docs/seal.md): How a report is sealed and how anyone re-verifies it offline; includes a worked test vector
- `POST https://analystos.dev/api/v1/verify`: stateless verification of any seal bundle, no account

## Identity and the FlashyOS mesh

- [Handshake](https://analystos.dev/.well-known/flashyos.json): flashyos/1
- [Charter](https://analystos.dev/.well-known/flashyos-charter.json): AAO 0.1, three roles, each with a measure
- [Mesh identity](https://analystos.dev/docs/mesh-identity.md): The handshake and charter AnalystOS publishes, and what it does not
- [AAO charter checking](https://analystos.dev/docs/aao.md): The FlashyOS AAO 0.1 charter checker, its rule codes and its limits

## Limits, stated plainly

- [Trust and known limits](https://analystos.dev/#trust): what leaves your environment, what is and is not checked
- Every figure is proven; only some relationships between figures are checked
- Sealing proves a report was built from the sealed facts, not that the facts are the important ones

## Optional
